$
\begin{aligned}
7000 \div 100                                &= 700 \div a \\\\
\dfrac{7000}{100}                            &= \dfrac{700}{a} \\\\
a \times \dfrac{7000}{100}                   &= 700 \\\\
a                                            &= \dfrac{700 \times 100}{7000} \\\\
a                                            &= \dfrac{7000 \times 10}{7000} \\\\
a                                            &= \dfrac{\cancel{7000} \times 10}{\cancel{7000}} \\\\
70                                           &= 10
\end{aligned}
$

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

If you add up the digits of $14$ you get $5$ i.e. $1 + 4 = 5$. How many $2$-digit numbers are there altogether (including $14$) which add up to a multiple of $5?$

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">If you add up the digits of $14$ you get $5$ i.e. $1 + 4 = 5$. How many $2$-digit numbers are there altogether (including $14$) which add up to a multiple of $5?$
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>

%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Multiples of $5 = 5, 10, 15, 20, \ldots$

$
\begin{aligned}
2\text{-digit numbers whose digits add upto } 5     &= 14, 23, 32, 41, 50 \\\\
2\text{-digit numbers whose digits add upto } 10    &= 19, 91, 28, 82, 37, 73, 46, 64, 55 \\\\
2\text{-digit numbers whose digits add upto } 15    &= 69, 96, 78, 87 \\\\
\text{Count}                                        &= 18
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$18$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

$\approx$ means approximately equal to. Given that $1\ \text{kilogram (kg)} \approx 2·2\ \text{pounds (lb)}$, convert $154\ \text{lb}$ to $\text{kg}$.

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">$\approx$ means approximately equal to. Given that $1\ \text{kilogram (kg)} \approx 2·2\ \text{pounds (lb)}$, convert $154\ \text{lb}$ to $\text{kg}$.
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
&= 154 \ \text{lb} \\\\
&= 154 \times \dfrac{1}{2.2} \ \text{kg} \\\\
&= \dfrac{154}{2.2} \\\\
&= \dfrac{154 \times 10}{2.2 \times 10} \\\\
&= \dfrac{154 \times 10}{22} \\\\
&= \dfrac{7 \times 22 \times 10}{22} \\\\
&= \dfrac{7 \times \cancel{22} \times 10}{\cancel{22}} \\\\
&= 7 \times 10  \\\\
&= 70 \ \text{kg}
\end{aligned} 
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$70 \ \text{kg}$

</div>
</div>

A powerful number has the property that for every prime number which divides into it, that prime number squared also divides into it.

e.g. $16$ is a powerful number because both $2$ and $2^2$ are factors.

&= 19
\end{aligned}
$

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

The competitors in the Tour de France cycling race are all given race numbers to wear. 
Based on last year's results, the captain of the leading team has the honour of wearing number $1$ and the other numbers of his 
team wear numbers $2$ to $9$.

![papers/dulwich-college/sample/specimen-paper-c/s01-q19-i00.png](/assets/papers/dulwich-college/sample/specimen-paper-c/s01-q19-i00.png "papers/dulwich-college/sample/specimen-paper-c/s01-q19-i00.png")

The captain of the next team in the rankings wears number $11$ and his team mates are given the race numbers from $12$ to $19$. 
The third team gets allocated the race numbers $21$ to $29$, and so on.

This process continues until all riders have been given a unique number that identifies them individually, but also identifies which team they are on.

</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Three bus services stop at my bus stop. Service $A$ departs every $3 \ \text{minutes}$, service $B$ every $5 \ \text{minutes}$ 
and service $C$ every $8 \ \text{minutes}$.

If all three services leave my stop at $10.00 \ \text{a.m.}$, at what time will they next leave my stop together? (Assume that all three services always run on time). 

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Three bus services stop at my bus stop. Service $A$ departs every $3 \ \text{minutes}$, service $B$ every $5 \ \text{minutes}$ 
and service $C$ every $8 \ \text{minutes}$.
<emptyline>
If all three services leave my stop at $10.00 \ \text{a.m.}$, at what time will they next leave my stop together? (Assume that all three services always run on time). 
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

LCM of $3, 5$ and $8 = 120$

After $120 \ \text{minutes}$, three bus services will leave the stop together.

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Time at which three services will next leave stop together}   &= 10{:}00 \ \text{a.m.} + 120 \ \text{minutes} \\\\
                                                                    &= 2{:}00 \ \text{a.m.}
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$2.00 \ \text{a.m.}$

</div>

**Question**

With which number must $4$ be **clotted** with to give $42?$

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">With which number must $4$ be **clotted** with to give $42?$
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the number $= a$

$42$ written backwards = $24$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
4 \times a &= 24 \\\\
a          &= \dfrac{24}{4} \\\\
a          &= \dfrac{6 \times 4}{4} \\\\
a          &= \dfrac{6 \times \cancel 4}{\cancel 4} \\\\
a          &= 6
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$6$

**Question**

Which statement is true?

-  $24 \times 70 = 48 \times 35$

-  $24 \times 70 = 12 \times 35$
-  $24 \times 70 = 48 \times 140$

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Here are $2$ number machines:

![papers/eltham-college/2019/sample-paper-1/s01-q20-i00.png](/assets/papers/eltham-college/2019/sample-paper-1/s01-q20-i00.png "papers/eltham-college/2019/sample-paper-1/s01-q20-i00.png")

Both machines have the same input.
Work out the input if both machines also have the same output.

- $2$
- $-2$
- $6$
- $-6$

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

<emptyline>
%image%
<emptyline>

<emptyline>
- $2$
- $-2$
- $6$
- $-6$
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Output of machine A       $= (n \times 4) + 4$

Output of machine B       $= (n \times 5) - 2$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
(n \times 4) + 4                                 &= (n \times 5) - 2 \\\\
4n + 4                                           &= 5n -2 \\\\
4 + 2                                            &= 5n - 4n \\\\
n                                                &= 6
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

$36$ is a square number because it can be written $6 \times 6$.

Similarly, $64 = 8 \times 8$ is a square number.

$1000$ is a cube number because it can be written $10 \times 10 \times 10$

Similarly, $343 = 7 \times 7 \times 7$ is a cube number.

The French mathematician Pierre de Fermat claimed correctly that there is only one square number that is $2$ less than a cube number.

It is less than $50$.

What is it? 

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">$36$ is a square number because it can be written $6 \times 6$.
<emptyline>
Similarly, $64 = 8 \times 8$ is a square number.
<emptyline>
$1000$ is a cube number because it can be written $10 \times 10 \times 10$
<emptyline>
Similarly, $343 = 7 \times 7 \times 7$ is a cube number.
<emptyline>
The French mathematician Pierre de Fermat claimed correctly that there is only one square number that is $2$ less than a cube number.
<emptyline>
It is less than $50$.
<emptyline>
What is it? 
</code></pre>
</div>

Square numbers less than $50 = 1, 4, 9, 16, 25, 36, 49$

Cube numbers less than $50 = 1, 8, 27$

$25$ is the square number which is $2$ less than the cube number $27$.
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

The next term is calculated by subtracting $3$ to the previous term. Hence, the sequence would be:

$
\begin{matrix}
&   \footnotesize {\maroonC {(-3)} } 
&&  \footnotesize {\maroonC {(-3)} }

28,  &&  25,  &&  22,  &&  19,  &&  16,  &&  13,  &&  10,  && \ldots,  &&  \ldots
\end{matrix}
$

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{First missing number}       &= 10 - 3 \\\\
                                  &= 7 \\\\
\text{Second missing number}      &= 7 - 3 \\\\
                                  &= 4
\end{aligned}
$

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

My calculator is broken. The only buttons that work are these.

$
\large {
\boxed{4}      \quad
\boxed{7}      \quad
\boxed{\times} \quad
\boxed{-}      \quad
\boxed{=}
}
$


Which sequence of buttons will enable me to get an answer of $11$ on the screen of my calculator?

If you have time, try to find some more ways to get $11$.

\end{aligned}

**Question**

Amran wrote down the calculation:

$\dfrac{6000 \times 20} {30} = 40$

Her teacher looked at the answer and said it could not be correct.

Explain how her teacher knew the answer must be wrong.

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

<emptyline>

</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$\dfrac{6000 \times 20} {30} = 40$

Lets verify.

$
\begin{aligned}
&= \dfrac{6000 \times 20} {30} \\\\ 
&= \dfrac{30 \times 200 \times 20} {30} \\\\
&= \dfrac{\cancel{30} \times 200 \times 20} {\cancel{30}} \\\\
&= 200 \times 20 \\\\
&= 4000
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>

<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
